conventions.pagination_hint: {shown} of {total} matches shown, call again with offset={next_offset} to see the rest

tools.name: discover_tools
tools.embedded_txt: Search for and discover additional tools beyond the static core set. Use when the current 7 tools are insufficient for the task. The discovery uses semantic embedding search to find tools matching your described capability needs. Returns tool schemas that get appended to the available tool set for the session. Examples: need to delete a file, query traceability graph, get code symbols, run specialized analysis. Call with a natural language description of what you need to accomplish.
tools.short_help: discover_tools(query, max_results?) — Find and load additional tools by capability.
examples: Find a tool to delete files
What tools can query the trace graph

tools.name: list_directory
tools.embedded_txt: List files and directories in a given path. Supports pagination via offset/max_results, recursive listing, glob filtering, and depth limiting. Use to explore project structure, find files by pattern, or browse directory contents. Returns file names with type indicators (trailing / for dirs). Replaces old non-paginated list_files. Examples: list all .rs files in src/, show project root structure, find all test directories recursively.
tools.short_help: list_directory(path?, recursive?, max_results?, offset?, file_filter?, max_depth?) — List files/dirs. Paginated.
examples: What files are in the root
Show me the files in this project

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search files with auto regex or semantic similarity. regex mode: fast pattern/text matching (case-insensitive fallback by default) — use for exact symbols, strings, comments, imports; escape special chars like . * ( for a literal match. semantic mode: natural-language, meaning-based search using embeddings — use for finding concepts, similar logic, or when a regex search returns no results. auto: tries regex first (then case-insensitive); if both fail, falls back to semantic.
tools.embedded_txt: Unified search tool combining regex grep and semantic embedding search. Regex mode: fast text/pattern matching across files like grep, for exact symbols, strings, comments, imports — escape special chars like . * ( for literal matches; falls back to case-insensitive automatically. Semantic mode: natural language search using embeddings, finds code by meaning not exact text — use for concepts, similar logic, or when regex finds nothing. Auto mode tries regex, then case-insensitive, then semantic, and reports which strategy produced the results. Supports pagination via offset/max_results, file filtering by glob, case sensitivity, context lines around matches. Use instead of run_shell for any file search task. Examples: find all TODO comments, search for authentication handling logic, locate where a function is defined, find files importing a module.
tools.short_help: find(query, mode?, case_sensitive?, max_results?, offset?, path?, file_filter?) — Search files by regex or semantic; auto falls back regex → case-insensitive → semantic.
examples: Search for fn main in src/

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read file lines from offset. Returns file metadata (lines, bytes, size, modified, permissions, owner, group). Empty range = metadata only.
tools.embedded_txt: Read lines from a file with pagination support. Returns content plus file metadata: total lines, bytes, human-readable size, relative modification time, unix permissions string, owner and group. Reading with max_results=0 returns only metadata without content — use as a cheap stat check. Supports negative offset (-1 = last line). Paginated: check has_more and next_offset in response data. Lines over 300 chars are truncated with a hint to re-read that specific line. Subsumes old count_lines tool since metadata always includes line count. Examples: read first 50 lines of main.rs, check file size without reading content, read last 20 lines of a log file.
tools.short_help: read_file(path, offset?, max_results?) — Read file lines. Paginated. max_results=0 returns metadata only.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace line range [start, end) with text. start==end inserts. Both omitted replaces whole file. Creates file if not exists.
tools.embedded_txt: Edit a file by replacing a line range with new text. Versatile: start==end means pure insert at that line (no removal). Both start and end omitted means replace entire file content. If file does not exist, creates it. Supports negative indexing (-1 = last line). Use for: inserting code at specific locations, replacing function bodies, creating new files, appending content. For single unique-string replacements, prefer replace_str instead. To edit multiple occurrences in one pass, apply the edits back-to-front — highest line number first — so earlier line numbers don't shift. Examples: insert import at line 0, replace lines 5-10 with new implementation, create a new config file, append test at end of file.

start.description: First line to replace (inclusive). Negative = from end.

end.description: Last line to replace (exclusive). Negative = from end.

tools.short_help: edit_file(path, text, start?, end?) — Replace line range [start,end) with text. start==end inserts; omit both to replace whole file.

tools.name: replace_str
tools.description: Replace a unique string occurrence in a file. Fails if not exactly one match; failure errors include line numbers of near/duplicate matches — use them with edit_file as the fallback.
tools.embedded_txt: Find and replace an exact string in a file. The old_str must match exactly once in the file — fails with error if zero or multiple matches found. On failure the error lists the closest matching lines (0 matches) or every match's line number (multiple matches); fall back to edit_file with those line numbers when the string can't be made unique. This is the safest edit operation when you know the exact text to change. Preferred over edit_file for: renaming functions/variables, fixing typos, updating import paths, changing single values. Does not use regex — literal string match only. Examples: rename a function, fix a typo in a comment, update a dependency version string, change a constant value.

old_str.description: Exact text to find (must match once).
old_str.error_hint: old_str must match the file's text byte-for-byte (including whitespace/indentation) and occur exactly once; read_file the relevant lines first if unsure.

tools.short_help: replace_str(path, old_str, new_str) — Replace exact string in file (must match exactly once).

tools.name: run_shell
tools.description: Run a shell command. Output truncated to head/tail lines.
tools.embedded_txt: Execute an arbitrary shell command in the project directory or specified cwd. Returns stdout and stderr with head/tail truncation for large outputs. Use for: running tests, building projects, installing dependencies, git operations, any CLI tool. Prefer find tool over run_shell for file searching. Timeout configurable (default 30s). Output shows first N and last M lines with a note about omitted middle. Examples: cargo test, npm install, git status, python script.py, make build.
tools.short_help: run_shell(command, cwd?, timeout_secs?) — Run shell command in project root.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web. Returns result titles and URLs; fetch one with web_fetch.
tools.embedded_txt: Search the web with a terms query (DuckDuckGo backend). Returns a list of result titles and URLs. To read a page's content, pass one of the returned URLs to web_fetch, which saves the page text into the project (.tracelean/web/) where read_file and find can inspect it. Use for: looking up library documentation, error messages, API references, current information not in the codebase. Examples: search for tokio watch channel docs, look up a compiler error, find the latest reqwest API.

query.description: Search terms (or a full http(s):// URL, which is fetched directly).

tools.short_help: web_search(query, max_results?) — Search the web; returns result titles + URLs.
examples: Search for tokio watch channel docs
Look up the latest reqwest API

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a URL; its readable text is saved to a project temp file for read_file/find.
tools.embedded_txt: Fetch a web page by URL. The page is downloaded, HTML is stripped to readable text, and the result is saved under .tracelean/web/ inside the project. The tool returns the saved path, line count, and a short preview — use read_file or find on that path to inspect the content. Use after web_search returns candidate URLs, or directly when you already know the URL. Examples: fetch https://docs.rs/tokio, download a changelog page, read an API reference page.
tools.short_help: web_fetch(url) — Fetch a URL as text into .tracelean/web/ readable with read_file/find.

tools.name: help_tool
tools.description: Get detailed usage info for any tool by name.
tools.embedded_txt: Retrieve the extended description (embedded_txt) for any available tool. Use when you need more detail about a tool's capabilities, parameters, edge cases, or usage examples before calling it. Works for both static and dynamic tools. Returns the full embedded_txt field which contains comprehensive usage documentation. Examples: help_tool('edit_file') to understand line range semantics, help_tool('find') to understand mode differences.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool to get help for.

tools.short_help: help_tool(tool_name) — Get detailed usage info for any tool.

dynamic_tools.name: delete_file
dynamic_tools.description: Delete a file. Reversible via undo.
dynamic_tools.embedded_txt: Delete a file from the filesystem. The operation is reversible through the undo system. Use when you need to remove files that are no longer needed: temporary files, deprecated modules, generated artifacts. Will fail if the path is a directory. Examples: remove a scratch file, delete an obsolete test, clean up generated output.
dynamic_tools.short_help: delete_file(path) — Delete a file (reversible via undo).

dynamic_tools.name: query_trace_graph
dynamic_tools.description: Query traceability graph by requirement ID. Returns linked specs, code, tests.
dynamic_tools.embedded_txt: Query the project traceability graph for a specific requirement. Returns all linked artifacts: formal specs (Lean4), implementing code elements (functions, structs), and test cases. Use to understand requirement coverage, find what code implements a requirement, or check test coverage for a feature. The trace graph is built from source annotations and spec files. Examples: what code implements REQ-01, show test coverage for REQ-03, find the formal spec for a requirement.
dynamic_tools.short_help: query_trace_graph(req_id) — Linked specs, code, tests for a requirement.

dynamic_tools.name: query_code_element
dynamic_tools.description: Query trace graph for a code element to find linked requirements and specs.
dynamic_tools.embedded_txt: Query the traceability graph starting from a code element (function, struct, module) to find which requirements it satisfies and which formal specs verify it. Use for impact analysis: before modifying code, check what requirements would be affected. Also useful to understand the purpose of unfamiliar code. Examples: what requirement does the login function satisfy, find the spec for the upload handler, check which reqs are impacted by changes to auth.rs.
dynamic_tools.short_help: query_code_element(file, name) — Requirements/specs linked to a code element.

dynamic_tools.name: list_requirements
dynamic_tools.description: List all project requirements with ID, title, and status.
dynamic_tools.embedded_txt: List all requirements defined in the project. Returns each requirement's ID, title, and current status (implemented, pending, partial). Use to get an overview of project scope, find requirements to work on, or check overall progress. No parameters needed — returns the complete list. Examples: show all project requirements, what requirements exist, check implementation status.
dynamic_tools.short_help: list_requirements() — List all requirements with ID, title, status.

dynamic_tools.name: get_symbols
dynamic_tools.description: Get parsed symbols (functions, structs, classes) from a file using tree-sitter.
dynamic_tools.embedded_txt: Parse a source file using tree-sitter and extract all top-level symbols: functions, structs, classes, traits, enums, constants, type aliases. Returns symbol name, kind, and line range. Use to understand file structure without reading the entire file, find specific functions by name, or get an overview of a module's API. Supports: Rust, Python, C++, JavaScript, TypeScript, Lean4. Examples: what functions are in auth.rs, show the struct definitions in types.rs, list all classes in a Python module.
dynamic_tools.short_help: get_symbols(path) — Parsed symbols (functions, structs, classes) from a file.
